result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.global_efficiency()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the global efficiency of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24193-L24253){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.global_efficiency() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Global efficiency is the average efficiency over all pairs of nodes, where efficiency is the multiplicative inverse of the shortest path distance. It measures how efficiently information flows through the network. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The global efficiency (between `0` and `1`). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - returns `0` for graphs with `0` or `1` nodes - returns `1` for complete graphs - unweighted shortest paths are used (all edge weights = 1) - for disconnected node pairs, efficiency is `0` - related to the average inverse distance ## Examples {.doc-examples} A complete graph has every pair of nodes directly connected, so its global efficiency is at its maximum of 1: ::: {#2962fccf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() n = 5 for i in range(n): graph.add_node(label=f"n{i}") nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) for i in range(n): for j in range(i + 1, n): graph.add_edge(nodes[i], nodes[j]) # Returns close to 1.0 graph.global_efficiency() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: ::: Sparser topologies have longer average shortest paths and therefore lower efficiency; a star graph is much more efficient than a path of the same size, since every node is at most 2 hops from any other through the hub: ::: {#484b9d2e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph() path.add_path_graph(10) star = ec.Graph() star.add_star_graph(10) # Path efficiency is much lower than star efficiency (path.global_efficiency(), star.global_efficiency()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.4286596119929453, 0.6) ``` ::: :::
